incident_description: I bought my six-month old son the Fisher Price piano toy (model BFH93) and he loves playing with it. I kept hearing a rattle from the toy. One day he was shaking it and a little piece of plastic shaped like a "T" fell out of the back of the toy. He grabbed it and I had to pry it out of his fist. It was about to go in his mouth. The piece is about 1/2 inch long and 0.365 inches wide at the top.  This is NOT safe for babies!!!! I have the piece and can send photos.
justification: A small plastic piece fell out of the toy and the child almost put it in their mouth, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
(08/13/2015) The consumer stated that her granddaughter got her finger on her right hand caught in the satin ribbon of the bib that is around the neck of the toy monkey. The child had played with the toy before.

There was no physical injury, but the child's finger was tangled in the ribbon and her finger was a dark purple.

No medical attention was required.
justification: The child's finger was tangled and turned dark purple, indicating a potential injury, but no medical attention was required.

incident_description:
I had already filed a report but due to the continuing problems with my left thumb I had to be seen at the local emergency room and I have a fracture resulting from this defective product.
[REDACTED]
I am left handed this is a huge set back they told me I should not work or go to school until my thumb is healed because the fracture is right by the joint which is not good at all.
justification: The description indicates a fracture requiring emergency room treatment and work/school restrictions, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as fractures from defective products are not extremely rare but not guaranteed.

incident_description:
Bath toys by elegant baby are very dangerous.
Even by following their instructions, these toys developed bacteria and rot all over their insides.
Babies play with these toys in the bath and regularly suck on them while parents do not realize their babies are being poisoned.
justification: The description indicates that babies are being poisoned by bacteria in bath toys, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: 6 month old boy admitted to the hospital after his 3 y/o sister fed him a bottle of Visine (tetrahydrozoline hydrochloride). Child required medications to increase heart rate, and child was intubated. Child hospitalized overnight in the intensive care unit.
justification: The child required medical intervention and hospitalization in the ICU, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
I bought Disney's Baby Stuffed Winnie the Pooh blocks for my son because they were adorable. My son is 8 months old and was playing with one of the cubes.  Luckily, I was right next to him.  I 
noticed that he was chewing on what I thought was a piece of tape.  It was the small crinkle plastic inside Pooh's arm tag!  He chewed through it (he ONLY has his 2 bottom teeth!) and if I wasn't there could have choked on the plastic! I am surprised that this happened with a Disney product.  I would expect higher quality.  Later, I noticed that the arm of the Tigger block (they come in a pack of three blocks) had become detached.  He won't be playing with these anymore!  I would also hope that there may be a recall issued so no other baby has the same sort of accident with a more tragic outcome...
justification: The child could have choked on the plastic but was unharmed due to parental supervision, indicating a potential hazard without actual injury.

incident_description: We were given a Magic Bouncy Ball making kit as a gift.  After completing the project, we stored the balls in a plastic resealable bag so they would not dry out and become to hard to bounce properly, as per instructions.  Two weeks later I started finding the balls in the house with mold on them and promptly threw them away.  I thought it was because they were not kept properly in the bags, but then I found the ones we stored properly in the bags with mold on them as well.  I thought the product would be like a regular quarter machine bouncy ball that could be kept forever, but this is not something I would let children play with and have the possibility they would ingest mold.  My kids are disappointed I had to throw away their creations.
justification: Mold on bouncy balls poses a potential health risk if ingested, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: My almost 2 year old was playing with her vtech move and crawl ball that she has had for over a year now. She had her ball and was walking around the house and she walked into the kitchen. I heard a pop so I went in to see what had happened and a chunk was missing from the ball and wires were exposed from the internal motor of the ball. It was still moving, making noise, and lighting up. I checked it, and it appears that when she dropped it, one of the animals that you can push popped out and exposed the wiring mechanism for the ball. I was shocked that it did this. I don't think that an infant toy should have wires that are so easily exposed. When I called vtech, they didn't seem concerned in the least bit about exposed wires in an infant toy.
justification: Exposed wires in an infant toy pose a potential hazard, but no injury occurred in this incident.

incident_description: When I attempted to remove the stroller from my car, my finger became caught, cut and bruised.  I am certain that if I had not managed to loose my finger with a maneuver using my other hand, that my finger would have been broken or partially amputated.
justification: The description indicates a finger injury (cut and bruised) with potential for worse outcomes (broken or partially amputated), warranting a severity level of 3.

incident_description: My two year old was playing with the battery powered train to the vtech go go train station.  I heard a loud pop and he started crying and ran to me holding his eye.  I looked at his eye and it was red on the inside lid and there was a little spot where it was blood shot on the white of his eye.  I took the train out of his hand and pushed power and it still worked.  I opened it up to take the batteries out and saw that one of the three batteries had exploded and there was battery acid all over the inside of the compartment.  I cleaned his eye and surrounding area well and it doesn't seem like it's a serious burn but it's pretty raw still. I reported to vtech and they said they don't have any injury reports with this train.  I had two different brands of battery in the train.  Two fusion and one [REDACTED].  The [REDACTED] is the one that exploded.  The vtech guy told me they recommend not mixing brands.  I told him that if mixing battery brands would cause them to explode there should be huge warnings on every toy.
justification: The child suffered an eye injury from a battery explosion, but it was not life-threatening. Battery explosions are uncommon but can occur when mixing brands.

incident_description: I wanted to report that I received a fishing game from Janod.com. The Ref. is [REDACTED] and the bar code is 3700217381523. The tin says that it is for 2-5 year olds and not suitable for those under 18 months due to a long cord strangulation hazard. No mention of magnets. When my son was playing with it, the worm on the end of one of the fishing poles suddenly popped apart and a small, powerful magnet fell out. When I noticed this, I looked at the other pole and the worm easily popped apart revealing a second small, powerful magnet. My son did not put these in his mouth, thankfully. This is a serious life threatening hazard. It appears that Janod.com is not a U.S. company but I received the game in my monthly subscription from Citrus Lane, citruslane.com and they appear to be based in CA. Thanks for your time.
justification: The incident involved a potential hazard with no actual injury, and the likelihood is possible as the magnets were discovered but not ingested.

incident_description:
The car seat adapter for our Baby Jogger City Mini stoller, popped off the stroller at the connection points flipping the carseat and my 2-month old baby girl to the pavement. 

We have owned the stroller and adapter for 2 1/2 years. We used it with our son when he was an infant without incident. My husband attached the adapter and carseat before our walk.  As we were leaving our driveway, the front wheel of the stroller bumped a lawn sprinkler head and the impact was enough to jolt the carseat adapter and attached carseat to the pavement. The carseat flipped forward and landed upside down. I immediately unstrapped my daughter and cradled her screaming little body to my own. I held her tightly rocking and screaming, "Oh my God, Oh my God, that should not have happened, what happened?"  We took her to an urgent care pediatric office where she was examined and no noticeable signs of injury are apparent. We are watching her closely for the next 48-hours for any signs of a head injury.
This should not have happened.
justification: The baby was examined and no immediate injuries were found, but potential head injury is being monitored, indicating a severity level of 3 due to the risk of injury.

incident_description: Child's battery operated [REDACTED]/sword. Owned for >6 months and batteries went dead. Replaced batteries this AM. This afternoon, 6 year old son was playing with the light saber and left it "on" lying on the rug. Picked it up a few minutes later and came running into the other room complaining that the handle was "hot." At this time observed the battery compartment of the handle to be emmiting smoke and could see charred portion of a wire protruding with the insulation melted/charred off. Immediately turned the device to the "off"position and opened the battery compartment and removed the batteries. The smoking stopped. Noted that the interior portion of the battery compartment in the handle was charred and the wires from the power switch to the battery terminal were charred with burnt insulation in their entirety.
justification: The incident involved smoke and charring but no injury occurred.

incident_description: We have the Uppababy Vista Stroller 2015 with the Rumble Seat attachment and use for my 7 month old and 2 year old (weights 18 and 22 pounds respectively). We were in a picnic and my 2 year old daughter was sitting in the rumble seat and leaned forward slightly and the whole attachment of the stroller where she was sitting fell. She hit her head on a wood fence and has a sizable hematoma. She could not put her hands to stop her since she was strapped in and had the bar attachment on.
justification: The 2-year-old suffered a sizable hematoma from hitting her head, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My 21 month old daughter managed to take off the ear piece on the Doc McStuffins stethoscope. No injuries sustained. Potential choking hazard.
justification: The child removed a small part without injury, but it presents a potential choking hazard.

incident_description: The front wheels collapsed underneath the stroller with two kids in it while they were being pushed across the street. The older child, a toddler, was standing on the deck. The infant was secured in the seat in front.
justification: The incident involved a stroller collapse with children, likely causing injury to at least one child given the description.

incident_description: The incident involves a Fisher Price Soothe and Glow Seahorse toddler toy. I was replacing the batteries in it, once they were installed, I tested the toy and it turned on just fine, so I put the battery case cover back on and screwed the two screws. I installed the battery case part back inside the soft body of the toy, turned it on, but it did not turn on. I removed the battery case part from the soft body, and that is when I noticed a sharp smell of burning plastic, and noticed the battery case lid was warm to the touch. I frantically unscrewed the two screws, and saw visible sparks at the negative terminal end of one of the batteries as I pulled it out. The battery was very hot to the touch, as was the case near that terminal end, the spring was compressed and blackened where before it had been normal just before installing the new batteries, and the plastic around that terminal end was melted and brownish.
justification: The incident involved sparks and burning plastic but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The clip on the car seat is easily unbuckled by an infant. My son is 6 months old and he has unclipped the buckle numerous times which unsafe for him.
justification: The infant can unbuckle the car seat, which is unsafe but has not resulted in injury yet.

incident_description: This has happened several times.  Any time the stroller meets a small crack while walking, the front wheels catch on it and stop abruptly.  The stroller tips forward violently and the person pushing it falls forward also.  The initial impact is very violent to both the baby and adult pushing, and then it's also dangerous if the stroller were to tip over completely and the person fall on top of the baby, which is very easy to do.
justification: The description indicates violent impacts and potential for injury to both the baby and adult, but does not confirm actual injuries or deaths.

incident_description: My 7 yr old son bought a stuffed Geoffrey giraffe (toyrus mascot) from toysrus.  He put it around his neck to carry it around and within hours he broke out into a bad bad rash on his neck and arms.  I took him to the doctor and they said he had a chemical reaction to something on the giraffe.  They put him on prednisone (RX) for 10 days to stop the reaction.  I am very concerned about what chemicals they are putting on our kids toys and stuffed animals.
justification: The child suffered a chemical reaction requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Today my son was thrown a Mini Beamo 16" Flying Hoop.  It hit him in the face at eye level, as it was spinning towards him.  The toy broke the skin left of his left eye, as well as severing the bridge of his nose.  He required 4 stitches to reattach his nose below the laceration.  The physician told us his cartilage was severed and that the wound will be at risk of infection until healed.  

The flying hoop toy was thrown to him by a 5 year old boy.  His parents purchased the toy 48 hours prior.  The toy is a fabric and foam wrapped fiberglass hoop, with a splinter revealed and poking through the fabric.  The splintered piece of fiberglass mostly like cut my son's face and nose.

Numerous customer reviews posted on Amazon.com reflect that the durability of this product is insufficient for lasting more than a day or two.  In my son's case, he nearly lost his eye sight, and we will be fortunate if he just gets away with a scared face.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring stitches and posed a risk of infection, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern, 
I have a Kolcraft Jeep jogging stroller that was purchased as a gift for my daughter's first birthday [REDACTED], but we did not use it until the last month or so because of her size. When we took it out and used it one night she climbed out and pushed down on the child tray snapping it off completely from the frame. I do not believe a 19lb child should be able to snap formed plastic in half and from a frame. Therefore I feel the product was defective. I have been in contact with Kolcraft customer service about this problem and their solution is for me to purchase another stroller. I feel they are overlooking this safety concern. 
I just wanted someone to listen to my  concerns for children.
Thank you for your time. 
Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The child was able to snap the plastic tray off the stroller, indicating a potential safety hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My daughter was sitting in her Minnie Mouse Big Wheel tricycle and stuck her hand in one of the holes behind the seat. There are 3 different settings to adjust the backrest of the seat and hers is the closest to the pedals. Behind that are 2 other holes on each side and she stuck her hand in one, all the way up to her wrist and it got stuck. We had to lay on the floor, squeeze her hand and pull from the top just to get her hand out. It took off the skin on each side of her hand and on top of it as well. They need to make covers for the holes not being used. Someone is going to really get hurt if this happens again. We were just lucky she didn't need to get it cut off.
justification: The incident resulted in skin injuries to the child's hand, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: I have purchased the 22" Plush Rocking Chair Rhino by Hugfun from Costco. The toy is really unbalanced and easily tilts backwards and causes the rider to fall back. The toy falls on the rider. My daughter and her friends repeatedly fell backwards. At first I thought that they just don't know how to ride it but every single one had the same issue, repeatedly. It is dangerous not only for infants and toddlers but also older pre-school kids.
justification: The toy causes repeated falls, posing a risk of injury to children, as described by multiple incidents of falling.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the tray that come across the front of the stroller while the car seat is in the stroller does not fasten securely which causes the car seat to fall forward and cause the child to fall out, no injuries were sustained.  

Caller stated that because of this incident the child has not been placed in the stroller or car seat again.  The manufacturer was contacted and they advised her that they were unable to assist her.

Caller is concerned that the stroller is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved the child falling out of the stroller but no injuries were sustained, and the likelihood is possible as the issue is with the stroller's design.

incident_description: We purchased a Baby Jogger City Select stroller in August 2013 and within six months we began noticing a violent shaking of the front wheels intermittently while pushing the stroller. Over the past few months the shaking has become constant and is worse the faster you push the stroller. It's quite dangerous now crossing an intersection.  I submitted this information to the company and never heard back from them. There are dozens of other similar complaints on the reviews of this product on the companies website. There is a video of the issue on YouTube.
justification: The stroller's violent shaking poses a clear hazard, especially at higher speeds, but no injury is reported.

incident_description: Hape "First Pounder" this eight piece toy is marked for ages 12 months+, it includes six colorful pegs that are straight with out any top or bottom, perfect choking size, fits in a toilet paper tube.  I've had to get one of these out of my 17m son's mouth 4 times since I gave it to him.  I've boxed the toy back up.   The version then I saw at the stores has these pegs built like bolts with large curved tops, these do not .
justification: The pegs are a choking hazard and have been removed from a child's mouth multiple times, indicating a clear incident but no injury.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the safety seat belt for the car seat malfunctions causing the child to fall out.  She stated that her 5 weeks old grandchild had fallen out once, there was no injury, the seat belt does not fasten securely.  The manufacturer was contacted and they advised her that they were unable to assist her.


Caller feels that the car seat whenever it is used in the car or outside of the car is unsafe.
justification: The child fell out of the car seat due to a malfunctioning seat belt but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is high (4) as the caller reports the issue persists whenever the car seat is used.

incident_description:
Caller stated that he experienced similar problems of recall# 13-221, the inner tube exploded while he was pumping air in it for a few seconds. Hazard: The inner tube of the tire on the stroller can rupture causing the wheel rim to fracture and fly off as a projectile, posing a risk of bodily injury and property damage. 

He received bruises to his left arm from the sharp objects that became projectiles.  He administered first aid to his arm.  He stated that the noise from the explosion caused his ringing to his ear.  No medical attention was received.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller stated that he feels that the incident should be reported.
justification: The caller sustained bruises and ringing in the ear from the explosion, indicating an injury but no need for medical attention.

incident_description: My 15 month old daughter was in her Smart Trike when she leaned over the side to touch the wheel. The whole tricycle tipped over with her in it onto the ground.
justification: The tricycle tipped over, but there is no mention of injury, only an incident occurred.

incident_description:
SKU: 9B5C6080

The consumer states that as soon as she purchased the unit, the canopy of the stroller would swing to the back even when there was little wind. Even when fastened, when the baby would move forward, the seat would move forward as well. This is a problem because when the baby moves forward and the canopy of the stroller is out, he would bang his head on the metal bars holding the canopy. The consumer states that he has banged his head multiples times and what makes it worse is the fact that the metal bars of the canopy are covered with a slim fabric, thus not offering much protection.

06/15/2014 - The consumer states that the stroller has a forty-five-pound capacity. She was using her stroller with her baby inside it for approximate three months before the rubber in the handlebar ran all the way to the left.

The consumer states that there are two hinged loops on either side of the stroller that pose a safety hazard to consumers' babies. The consumer had to contact the manufacturer in order to understand how to remove these hinged loops, and was then informed that the instructions were included in the instructions manual.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.

When the consumer's one year old son is in the almost go position "\_", he is in danger because the canopy holders he hits alway
justification: The description indicates the baby has banged his head multiple times due to the stroller's design flaws, which constitutes an injury (severity 3). The issue occurs frequently when the baby moves forward, making it likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description: i need help with a baby safety issue.. i bought new carseat and stroller for a child and now i see that they are defective.. the latch on the stroller will not latch and the baby car seat the 5 point harness is not clipping so in the even of an accident the baby would not be restrained into the seat... i contacted the company  **BABY TREND** and they are telling me there is nothing they can do. this baby is 5 weeks old today  where do i turn for help
justification: Defective car seat and stroller could lead to injury in the event of an accident, especially for a 5-week-old baby.

incident_description: My 5 month old was playing with the toy on our bed. We had just bought the toy for her and we were watching to see if she enjoyed it or not. There are some discs on the toy and her fingers became wedged inbetween. She was not injured because we were able to remove her fingers from the toy immediately. If not, I'm sure it would have ended much worse.
justification: The child's fingers became wedged in the toy, but there was no injury as the parents intervened immediately.

incident_description: I bought this stroller in September and have only used it for three months, as I live in Montana and winters are harsh. Today I went jogging with it and the front wheel came off, and the frame collapsed sending me over the top of it and my baby to the concrete, thankfully the safety straps work.  I have cuts and bruises as well as my baby.
justification: The stroller failure caused injuries to both the parent and baby, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
o Whom This May Concern-

My wife and I bought the Britax BOB Revolution from REI about 7 months ago for our daughter who is now 9 months old. When I went to take her out of it today after a walk I found that the button that releases the two side straps was missing. After looking more closely I found that she was sitting on it. Please see the attached photo.

I don't have to tell you how serious a situation this could have been if she had found this small piece of plastic during our walk and swallowed it.

We hadn't noticed anything wrong with it prior to today. The only thing that occurred that was out of the norm was that I mistakenly had the center clasp that this button is in reversed when I first put her in the stroller and tried to clip her in. I noticed that the clips didn't seem right and realized what I did so I pulled them out and reversed the center clasp so it was in the correct position and then clipped her in. Not sure if this caused the button to fall out but if so it could easily happen to anyone. I'm very good with straps, ratchets, clips, etc. because of my line of work so it's not as though I'm unfamiliar with these types of things.

We are obviously concerned for our daughter's wellbeing as well as that of other children that ride in the same stroller.

Please let me know that you received this email and that the appropriate people are informed of what occurred.

Thank you,
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED] cell
justification: The incident involved a missing button that could have led to a choking hazard, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: While unfolding the umbrella stroller the latch seemed to miss locking and the hinge started folding in the opposite direction. I pushed it back to the center and the latch seemed to catch properly but when my daughter was placed in the stroller and we began walking the hinge started to fold downward again.
justification: The stroller malfunctioned but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The issue recurred, suggesting a possible likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: The tires on our Jeep stroller were low. My husband used his small, portable air compressor to fill a rear tire. The tire, including rim, exploded.
justification: The tire explosion is an incident with potential for injury, but the description does not mention any harm occurring.

incident_description:
This is about Ever Earth activity walker sold on amazon.com
http://www.amazon.com/EverEarth-30949-Activity-Walker/dp/B003DQJWH0/ref=cm_cr_pr_product_top?ie=UTF8
This toy looks so cute, but is very dangerous:
--Two of the wheels falls off. Constantly. While the child is pushing. As if that isn't alarming enough, it's attached with a small washer and screw.
I discovered this by finding the washer and the screw in my baby's mouth after my toddler tried it the first time. No matter what we do. When the toy gets pushed, the wheel unscrews right away. We installed the wheel exactly as it said on the package. We even took them all off and reinstalled them after it first happened.
--When babies try to stand up, holding on to the toy, it falls over. 
--The child goes right over the top of it when they run into an obstacle (such as an area rug) that stops the wheels. 
Please read the reviews on amazon to see that these are common issues with this toy. Its a really bad design, its dangerous and should be recalled!
It has a choking hazard warning on the amazon page, but this is a walker. Walkers are for babies around 12 months, learning to walk, not kids 3 years and older.
Thank you!
justification: The description indicates a choking hazard and potential for injury due to the toy's design flaws, with multiple reports of similar incidents.

incident_description: This is my second time writing a report about Schwinn jogging stroller. I wrote the same report last year around the same time and now the same exact thing happen to the replacement stroller they sent out. I was at Azalea Park in Roswell walking with my 2 year old daughter and my 4 year old was on her bike. I went to turn around after walking 2 and half miles and completely lost control over the stroller and it turned completely on its side because the front wheel came off. My 2 year screamed because it clearly scared her. With no front wheel attached there was no way to lift it up to a position to get her out of it. So I had to bend down and take her out of the safety harness. I woman came over to help me as I attempted to put the wheel back on but no luck because it was missing pieces.. I'm at a park and now I have to walk back carrying my two year old to my car which is 2 and a half miles away. Now the last time this happened the company wanted me to just throw the stroller away and this time I'm keeping it.. This is a danger.
justification: The stroller malfunction caused a scare but no injury, and this is the second occurrence of the same issue.

incident_description: I was assembling the toy bow and arrow for my daughter, and half of the bow snapped back and slammed my hand, causing serious pain. I tried to put it together again, but when it was clear the two pieces were not going to fit together properly in order to screw them together, I went to remove the two pieces. I stopped, not wanting to potentially injure my hand again, so I got scissors to cut the elastic rope that made the piece hit my hand so forcefully in the first place, knowing I would never allow my child to play with the toy because of its obvious hazards. When I cut the elastic string, it snapped so hard, it left welt marks on both of my thighs, through pants. At this point, I put the toy in a place no children would get to it and tried to call the company, but they were closed. Obviously, the tension in the elastic string is too great to have the consumer be responsible for assembling the bow and arrow. The pain is persisting into my wrist and I will follow up with my doctor if it continues to persist to see if anything is broken.
justification: The incident caused serious pain, welt marks, and potential wrist injury, indicating an injury severity level.

incident_description: The Fisher-Price Soothe and Glow Seahorse poses a fire hazard.  When changing the batteries (AA rechargeables, a total of 3), one of the battery coils heats up, burns hot to an orange color, and releases fumes.  This also causes the battery to heat up.  Both the coil and the battery are hot enough to burn the skin.  If left in the toy, the plastic would easily melt, and possibly start the toy on fire.
justification: The incident describes a fire hazard with potential for burns and property damage, but no actual injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: 2 tires were blown out  while child was in the stroller.
justification: The incident involved blown-out tires with a child in the stroller, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My  5 year old was playing with a Caterpillar Cement Truck with a Tethered Remote Control made by Toy State International Ltd. The toy is rated for 3+ ages. In the short time that I looked away, he wrapped the cord around his neck 4 times. When he stood to come and tell me about it, the weight of the truck and the remote control tightened. He was coughing and whimpering and couldn't figure out how to unravel the cord when he came to me. I quickly unwound the cord from his neck, and thankfully he was okay. There was a red mark around his neck for the next thirty minutes after the event. Thankfully Nothing terrible happened, but I can only imagine if he hadn't come to me right away. We have had several conversations prior to this about the dangers of cords around the neck, especially since he has younger siblings. I feel the age rating should be higher on toys with tethered remote controls, or perhaps the remote should simply be wireless.
justification: The child suffered a red mark and discomfort but no lasting injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The incident highlights a clear hazard with tethered toys, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely) if precautions aren't taken.

incident_description:
I was changing the batteries in my daughter's Hasbro Littlest Petshop Walkables baby tiger toy. I opened the back of the tiger's battery compartment and removed the batteries. Somehow one of the batteries exploded with a loud pop. I piece of metal flew off of the battery case and there was evidence of combustion (ash & smoke). Fortunately no one was injured, however my 9 year old was in the proximity and was frightened quite badly. I think this is not an isolated incident. I would like a refund on the toy, which was purchased at Target. I would also like you to consider a recall. I have reported this to the Consumer Products Safety Commission. I have retained the toy and the remnants of the battery. Please feel free to contact me.
Sincerely
[REDACTED]
justification: The battery explosion caused a loud pop, metal fragments, and smoke, but no injuries occurred, though a child was frightened.

incident_description:
I purchased a Wubble Ball for my daughter.
i carefully read the instructions regarding the inflation of the ball.
I finished inflating the ball, and set it on my bed, at which time, it abruptly, and violently popped in  her face.
I purchased another ball, and took it outside to inflate, and this one popped as well, with violent force. luckily, no one got hurt either time, but had my daughter been a baby, the force of the popping would certainly cause harm.
justification: The incident involved violent popping of the ball but no injuries occurred, though potential for harm was noted.

incident_description: 4 month old baby was playing with "kid II, inc oball Rollin rain stick" ball. Baby was able to push arm through ball opening and trap arm inside ball. Baby then tried thrashing it off, as a baby does, which made the situation worse and forced baby arm deeper inside and bent at an angle around the middle rattle/rain stick portion which could have harmed the baby if mother didn't notice. Ball then was extremely hard to get off because of normal baby's wrists shape with the extra fatty pudgey bit.
justification: The baby's arm was trapped and bent at an angle, which could have caused injury if not for the mother's intervention.

incident_description: My daughter has a Fisher Price Soothe and Glow Seahorse.  When my husband changed the batteries,  it started smoking and he burned his hand. incident_description:
The information below was taken from an email sent to the CPSC Information Center:

The consumer believes that his alcohol burners present the same exact problem as the ones in Recall# 06-061.

The consumer has 50 unsafe wick-less metal alcohol burners (used in scientific experiments).

Description: The metal alcohol burner consists of a stainless steel tank with a screw-on steel lid. A copper tubing wick in the shape of a loop is soldered on the top of the burner's lid. The burner and lid measure 3-inches in diameter by 3 ÃÂ½-inches high. The burner also has a separate metal top which fits over the copper wick to act as a snuffer, and a metal heat shield designed to sit on top of the lid. It has a rubber keeper to prevent vaporization of alcohol. The item number 97-5320 is printed on the burner's packaging. The possible name of the manufacture is ÃÂPremierÃÂ located in China (see photo of shipping container).  The shipping container has this information on it also: C.A PO. No.P182 BALTIMOR C/NO. MADE IN CHINA.  

A possible injury or property damage can occur due to flammable alcohol leaking from the holes located in the copper tubing on the upper coil portion of the burner. The holes are in a placement where the rubber keeper/stopper cannot prevent fuel from leaking out when tipped over or when the internal temperature of the fuel tank rises and forces fuel to rise upward through the copper tubes leading to the coil on the surface of the burner. (See photo of hole not being covered by rubber keeper/stopper) I have inspected 10 out of the 50 received and all have the same hole placement. (see photo of hole in relation to rubber keeper/stopper).  On or about March 21 is when I observed the alcohol leaking from the holes in the copper coil. At that time I notified the retailer of the problem. Their response was: ÃÂas to the product recall, we checked with the manufacturer and that was for a previous model, not this oneÃÂ. Dated: March 23, 2015 

On or about March 21, is when I searched the internet for information regarding this type of burner to see if anyone had experienced the fuel leakage problem. That is when I discovered there was a recall issued by CPSC. In that report it is stated that the alcohol was leaking from a soldered area at the base of the copper tube. In that report it was also stated that the package had the item number, 97-5320, on the burnerÃÂs package. That is the same number that is on the 50 packages that I received.   It seems the ÃÂrecalledÃÂ burners with the identification number, 97-5320, are being sold again in violation of the 2006 recall issued by CPSC. 

The commission states that it is illegal to resell or attempt to resell a recalled consumer product. I am prepared to ship the alcohol burners to CPSC, United States Consumer Product Safety Commission for their inspection and validation to my claim. Included in this claim are photos of: 1.My proof of purchase from Amazon .com/ by C and A Scientific via Medix Corp. 2. Photo of hole location on alcohol burner where fuel leaks in relation to rubber keep/stopper. 3. Photos of shipping container from Medix Corp. containing boxes of burners. 


I purchased them on March 3, 2015 (50 pcs.) see attached photo of purchase order via amazon.com filled by Medix Corp.  I suspect approximately 5-7 days after shipment they were delivered to my location.  All 50 were purchased at the same time.

They were shipped in 3 shipments:
3/4/15  (1 ea.)
3/9/15  (32 ea.)
3/17/15 (17 ea.)


I discovered the leak prior to using. I followed the instructions to test for leaks before using. I turned the burner upside down and the fuel leaked from under the rubber stopper. I continued to test the burner by igniting it. After testing for approx. 1/2 hour I blew out the flame. Shortly after that,  the fuel started to slowly ooze from the holes in the coil and puddle at the base of the copper tubes where the solder is affixed to the tubes. Evidently there is residual pressure inside the body of the burner which causes fuel to rise upward via the copper tubes that extend to the bottom of burner. The tubes have a wicking material inside of them which carries fuel upward by means of capillary action. That wicking material extends all the way up to the holes where the leaks occurred.  Because the body of the burner is very warm after extinguishing the flames, there is a positive pressure inside the fuel reservoir. That pressure pushes down upon the fuel and forces it up into the copper tubes. Because the rubber stoppers do not properly cover the 2 flame holes, it seeps out.

I am extremely concerned about these burners.  I need reassurance in some fashion that this will never happen again.  I will refrain from returning the burners to the Medix Corp., because. I fear they will not properly dispose of them.
justification: The incident involves flammable alcohol leaking from defective burners, posing a risk of property damage or injury, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Dear CPSC,
I purchased the toy called "Picasso Tiles" after seeing my two-year old play with it at a friend's place on a play date. Because of the colors and shapes, I thought it seemed like it would be an educational toy for her. Yesterday we received the toy through amazon.com, and played with it for the first (and only) time. During the time playing, I did not notice that one of the tiles came apart, spilling six tiny magnets. I am not sure when it split open. My daughter is two years old, so we were not throwing the tiles or playing with them in any odd way. I discovered that one of the tiles had opened when I started to clean up and put the tiles away, back in the Picasso Tiles box, and found only half a tile. I realized immediately that the magnets were no longer in the piece, and searched frantically for the six tiny magnets, worried that my very agile child would find them. Luckily I quickly located all six magnets. Shaken, I read the box, where there was a warning label stating that death could occur if the magnets are ingested - the magnets could cause the intestines to stick together. I couldn't believe that a product such as this is available for consumer consumption. It was the first time we had played with the toy, and one of the pieces had inadvertently fallen apart. I am very worried for other families who may not be aware of the dangers of this toy, and might leave their children alone to play with it, not realizing that this is a poorly made product and could spill magnets everywhere. (The magnets are so small that I had a hard time finding them - some were in the box, and some were stuck to other pieces.) The toy was very expensive, and the packaging nice, so one would assume that it is a high quality product. It is not. I am very fearful that little children could be harmed by this toy. I returned the toy to amazon.com today.
Thank you, [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a tile breaking and spilling magnets, but no injury occurred as all magnets were found before ingestion.

incident_description:
Needle found in Pillow Pet 
My 6 year old daughter sleeps with her Panda Pillow Pet almost every night.  One night as I was putting her to bed, I was resting on her pillow pet.  I brushed my hand across the pillow and felt something sharp.  My first thought was that it's a cactus thorn since we live in AZ.  I was wrong.  I felt it again and actually discovered a sewing needle in the face seam of the Panda Pillow Pet.  I couldn't believe it!  

I'm so glad that I found it instead of my daughter!  She could have been seriously injured!  Imagine if it poked her head, face, hands...  This is so horrible!  She could have found it by jumping on her bed, too!  What if it poked her foot or her leg!!  

Do I really need to investigate all of her pillows and stuffed animals for needles??  There is no way this should have happened!  

I even looked online to see if it's happened before and I actually found a report from a few years ago!  So, they've had this problem before and it wasn't corrected?  My children should not be put at risk by a pillow or a stuffed animal!  Good thing she sleeps in the middle of the pillow and not by the Panda's face where I found the needle.   I have the needle and the pillow pet.  I'm completely disappointed in this company.
justification: A needle was found in a child's pillow pet, posing a serious injury risk, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I wanted to make you aware of an incident that occurred with a game product.  We were at a friend's house and they have a corn-hole game.  Model number 76023. GR-1-03/10/2014.  This is the "ESPN College Gameday" one.   They had it set up outside as it is suppose to be.   My 10 year old daughter ran past the cornhole game to go to the swing set.  (She was not even playing the game)  and tripped and landed on the cornhole game.  The legs buckled and her finger became trapped between the leg and game.   It acted as a guillotine and almost completely amputated her right hand ring finger.  She had go to the ER and then had to have surgery 1 week later to insure that her nail bed would heal correctly and had to have a cast on for 4 weeks.  Mind you this is her right hand she writes with.  Thank God her finger looks perfect today and she is doing awesome.  I wanted to let you know this because I don't want it to happen to any other child.  This was a horrific ordeal for the entire family and our friends who had this in their yard.  The fear that she may lose a fingertip and having to go through surgery is nothing a ten year old should have to endure, not to mention the medical bills we incurred.  The legs should have some type of locking mechanism so they don't fold/buckle easily.  We thought this should be brought to your attention.  Thank you.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring ER visit and surgery, but no death occurred.

Once they were opened and air out the smell did not get better.  I looked on the package and it said to wash pieces with a damp cloth before use so I did that.
