Caller feels that this toy is a safety hazard to children and should be reported.

The consumer added the specific name of gun is Air Warriors Range Master Extreme, and Walmart's number is 552744694..Consumer also noted she does not have product anymore so she can't look on it for an actual serial number.
justification: The child's finger was swollen and bruised, indicating an injury, but no medical attention was required and the symptoms resolved within a few days.

incident_description: I picked my car seat up with my 2 month old in it, and while walking out of my door the handle of the carseat became unlocked and I almost dropped the baby and the carseat.
justification: The car seat handle became unlocked, but the baby was not dropped, indicating no injury occurred.

incident_description: My friend's toddler (2yo) was riding this toy and flipped forward resulting in his teeth cutting completely through his bottom lip. He is currently in the ER and will need stitches. Not even 15 minutes later MY child rode on this car and flipped it to the left resulting in crying. She got up and rode on it again and leaned forward WHILE SITTING DOWN and hit her head on the nearest object, being the leg of a wooden desk. I am reporting this toy because it was made for the ages of 1-3 and both children are 2 and were not playing rough on this toy and resulted in tears, bumps on the head, and an ER visit with stitches.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring ER visits and stitches, and another child experienced bumps and tears, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is high (4) as two separate incidents happened in quick succession under normal use.

incident_description:
On Feb. 24, 2015 our 18-month-old went down for a nap in her crib with her stuffed animal bunny. After a few minutes, our nanny reported seeing her sit up on the video monitor -- and then she saw our toddler put something in her mouth. Concerned, our nanny went in to investigate. 

The bunny's eye had fallen out -- a half-inch plastic screw -- and our 18-month-old daughter had put it in her mouth. Fortunately our nanny was watching on the monitor and our 18-month-old did not choke. No one was harmed but this story could have ended very differently.

The bunny is a white, plush, soft and snuggly baby toy. It was given to us as a gift between 2011 and 2014 (either for our older daughter's birth or for our younger daughter's birth) but I don't know where it was purchased or who gave it to us. It does, however, have a series of tags on it. Photos attached.

The bunny has a small tag that says it is for decoration, not meant as a toy. But ... really? It's very soft and snuggly and clearly a toy. I'd be happy to send it to you, along with the plastic eye. 

Nothing bad happened in our situation, but I felt compelled to report this lest another family not be so fortunate. Baby toys should not have screws for eyes!!
justification: The incident involved a potential choking hazard but no injury occurred due to timely intervention by the nanny.

incident_description: The cat eye came off.  My grandson is two.
justification: The cat eye coming off is an incident but there is no mention of injury, especially to the grandson.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the back base of the tricycle is a lot heavier than the front, which enables the tricycle to flip forward with the smallest of pressure being applied when in use. 

01/20/2015 (Approximate) The consumer's daughter was using her tricycle. Approximately five minutes later, her daughter fell head-first. She did not injure her head. She received bruising on her right leg. The consumer indicates that within ten minutes, her daughter and a neighbor's child fell using the unit.

The consumer states that her daughter has been falling off the tricycle ever since it was purchased. The consumer believes the design of the unit is faulty. The consumer also plans on returning the product to the retailer. 

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard. The consumer plans on contacting both the manufacturer and the retailer to inform them of the safety hazard this unit poses.
justification: The incident resulted in bruising, which qualifies as an injury, and the description indicates frequent falls.

incident_description: I purchased a Fisher Price 10 Piece Band Set + Bonus Monkey Piano for my friend's niece. There is a trumpet inside which a piece that is in the mouth piece, the "reed" I believe, came out.....we wouldn't have known this if we hadn't blown on it ourselves to show the child....when we inspected the toy, the part came out in our hand! This could have came out in the mouth of the child and choked him!
justification: The incident involved a small part detaching, posing a potential choking hazard, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: My two year old daughter was playing with her favorite doll today. She comes up to me and says "hot hot" so I take the doll from her and immediately burn my hand and drop the doll.  When I picked it back up, I noticed a scorched burn mark on the center of the chest.  In a panic, I yelled for my husband that our daughter's baby doll was on fire. He grabbed the doll and removed the batteries. We had no idea until a few minutes ago that it had been recalled.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the parent, and the doll was recalled, indicating a known hazard.

incident_description: I purchased the Fisher Price Little People House in December for Christmas. It has a piece that is like a baby cradle and shaped like a bird, with a very sharp pointy beak. A friend had it in her hand and while they were playing it poked her eye. It was centimeters from going into her eyeball. The design is very dangerous!
justification: The sharp beak caused an eye injury, which could have been severe if it had penetrated the eyeball.

incident_description: We purchased Crayola Doodlers Bath Gel Crayons at Target. While bathing my son, the gel accidentally got into his eye. It caused severe burning and irritation. We contacted poison control and they advised us to flush his eye with water for 15 minutes. We did that but it was still red and swollen. The following morning, his eye was still red and swollen. We took him to the doctor who said he got a bacterial infection from the gel.
justification: The gel caused severe burning, irritation, and a bacterial infection requiring medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My 14 month old son got his arm stuck in his little tikes dump truck ball chute trying to retrieve a "boulder" he placed inside causing lacerations on his wrist.
justification: The incident resulted in lacerations on the child's wrist, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: School bus got caught in child's hair and pulled big chunk of hair out of his head
justification: The incident describes a child's hair being pulled out by a school bus, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: We installed brand new batteries in the product per the box's instructions.Our toddler was playing with the product, when we noticed a black liquid seeping from the battery compartment. We immediately removed the toy from her hands and took off her clothing, which had gotten the liquid on it. We investigated the toy and discovered that one of the batteries had popped and was seeping battery acid. There was a puddle of it on our foam play floor, which was causing it to melt. Had we not caught our daughter in time, she may have ingested it or touched it.
justification: The incident involved battery acid leakage and potential harm, but no actual injury occurred as the child was removed in time.

incident_description:
Daughter was playing with a container/ tin that her new watch came in. The tin has a plastic window opening  in the front.  She pushed the plastic window back and sliced it on the edge of the tin. It was almost needed stitches. I've been a Medical Responder for years and while the blood loss was wasn't severe, I still had to work to control it. It finally quit weeping late last night. 

Upon further examination of the container, the edge is absolutely razor sharp.
justification: The daughter sustained a significant injury that almost required stitches, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
Had flown my son's toy helicopter for about 2-3 mins then went to charge it. It started smoking from the remote control. I have charged it before without issue. The batteries were essentially new with only a few uses on the helicopter. It seems the charging mechanism shorted out as the smoke was pouring out from the top of controller and the green LED light that indicates charging and the areas around it were hot. I pulled the batteries out and they were fine no heat or anything.

Product example here:
http://www.amazon.com/Black-Spider-XT-Spider-Remote-Helicopter/dp/B00A10DRUO

Product Info:
Black Spider-XT (tactical wireless indoor helicopter)
Date of Production: July 2014
Location: Shantou, China
Manufacturer: Ruichuang Toys Co, Ltd
Distributor: MTG, Inc., Addison, IL
justification: The incident involved smoke and heat from the remote control but no injury occurred, and the batteries were unaffected.

incident_description:
The toy train engine is battery operated and I bought it for my three year old grandson, a Thomas the Tank Engine fan. 
I picked it up to put it out for him to see because he would be visiting and playing with his trains and tracks. 
While holding the toy train engine in one hand, the "on" button was tapped, and unintentionally turned the toy on. The skin and soft tissue of my finger got pinched, stuck, and bruised in the turning wheels of the battery operated toy train engine. 
There is a risk of a greater injury happening on a baby's or toddler's small, tender fingers. I put it away so he doesn't see it or play with it. I am afraid he will get hurt by it.

I went online to check on injury reports on the model toy. I found comments on injury by seven persons that posted reviews on Amazon.com.  My injury results in at least eight incidents.
justification: The incident resulted in a bruised finger, indicating an injury (severity 3). Multiple similar injuries reported online suggest the occurrence likelihood is high (4).

incident_description: We assembled 3 HearthSong Hideaway Stands (729069) from www.hearthsong.como (also available through Magic Cabin and Amazon). The purpose of the product is to hang a decorative/play bower in a child's room or playroom. The stands flipped over multiple times with our kids playing under their bowers. All bowers were well within the 25lb weight limit (5 lbs and 7 lbs.). I cannot imagine that these stands can function safely and effectively for their intended purpose.
justification: The stands flipped over multiple times during use, posing a risk to children, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Happy's toy dog has twice now cut my child. The first incident was on her hand when she picked it up to turn it off. The cut was not extremely deep and from then on we told her to just not pick it up anymore. Then today she was playing with the toy dog and it ran over her toe slicing the tip of it.
justification: The toy dog caused cuts on the child's hand and toe, indicating an injury but not life-threatening.

incident_description: Arrma Raider XL BLX remote control car, once a battery was plugged into this I ran the vehicle and after 45 minutes the ESC(electronis speed control) overheated, smoked and burst into blue and red flames. I unplugged the battery and the wires from the ESC to the brushless motor where to hot to touch. I contacted Arrma customer support to report the incident .
justification: The incident involved an ESC overheating and catching fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: We purchased a bedtime glowing owl (it's a purple stuffed animal with lights on his belly)from Walmart in November 2014. It has the name Funhouse! On the tag, but I don't have the box. Federal rn# is 90347, delivery date is 05/2014. It wasn't working, I assumed the battery was dead, when I went to change the battery pack it was melted, luckily it didn't start a fire. These need to be pulled from shelves immediately. I do have photos for proof.
justification: The melted battery pack indicates a potential hazard, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: We purchased the Mirari Pop Pop Piano for my son.  The toy is rate for children 12 months and over according to the package, but the clear plastic casing on top of the piano is easily  removed.  My 4 year old removed the casing and within seconds my 7 month old had one of the jacks in his mouth, a clear choking risk.
justification: The incident describes a choking hazard due to a toy's easily removable parts, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
On 12/21/14 the submitter's daughter was playing with the toy when she pulled the plastic cover off and it hit her in the face. As the submitter's daughter was pulling the plastic cover it turned around and the bottom edge of the plastic cover hit her top lip causing a laceration. The submitter's daughter was playing with the toy for a few minutes before the incident occurred. The submitter was watching her daughter and saw the incident occur. The submitter did not seek medical attention for her daughter.

The submitter took the toy away from her daughter and put it on a table. However, the submitter's daughter was able to retrieve the toy from the table and began playing with the toy. When the submitter realized her daughter had already removed the plastic cover and was trying to put a jack inside her mouth. The toy has 6 tubes and each tube has a jack inside. 

The submitter plans to contact the firm after filing this report. 

The submitter feels the toy is not safe for children and is concerned that the jacks inside the tubes can be a choking hazard. 

The  submitter noted toy is on Amazon.com where similar complaints can be read...
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration to the child's lip, indicating an injury (severity 3). The recurrence of similar incidents and the child's ability to retrieve and misuse the toy suggest a likely occurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description: This toy has a component that is fired as a projectile in the normal course of using the item. The projectile has a pointed end that could injure an individual nearby.  The children using the toy hit their grandfather with the projectile and it had sufficient force that he brought it to my attention
justification: The projectile caused an incident with sufficient force to be noticed, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Musical Owl by Alex toys has two holes for the drum sticks - my 15 month old granddaughter got her thumb stuck in the hole.  Just thought might want to caution parents.  My husband bought pegs and filled the holes.
justification: The child got her thumb stuck in the toy's hole, indicating an incident but no reported injury.

incident_description: I recently took my son for a walk in his Graco Stroller and the hinge on the side pinched his finger and caused him to bleed pretty bad. I had to run him to the ER and he had to get stitches! I am taking it back but don't know how or where. I am also in the process of a lawsuit but don't know if it will go anywhere. I am warning everyone I know not to buy Graco. I used to love their products.
justification: The child suffered an injury requiring stitches, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the description of the incident.

incident_description: My daughter has (had) the seal glow pet. she was laying down resting when she noticed it smelt gross, this is when I discovered that the on switch was very hot to the touch and did smell of an electrical fire . I examined the on switch by cutting the fabric open and discovered that the switch had melted, brown marks on the wires. I am glad I caught it when we did and it did no harm to my child. if it would have gone un-noticed I fear that things could have been much worse.
justification: The incident involved a melted switch and signs of an electrical fire, posing a clear hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I was set my baby on the ground on a blanket next to the bathroom with a few baby toys, including the rattle I am reporting. While I went to the bathroom she had wiggled so that she was not facing me but still within my reach. I noticed she started making a gagging sound and I pulled the end of this rattle out of her mouth as it had completely blocked the opening of her mouth and had passed her gums into the center of her mouth. If she were further away from me or had a completely clogged sinus pathway she could have suffocated.
justification: The baby was unharmed but the incident could have led to suffocation if circumstances were different.

incident_description:
(11/29/2014) The consumer stated that she had the baby in the stroller walking through the store. She noticed that the stroller was leaning to the right. She checked the tires and noticed that the back right tire had popped. She also noticed that the back left was damaged. 


The consumer also stated that the car seat that is a part of the travel system, gets stuck in the stroller at times.
justification: The stroller had a popped tire and damage, but no injury was reported, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a Graco LiteRider click connect stroller about a week ago. Over the course of the week, I noticed that the brakes were engaged, but either wouldn't catch when engaged or would release on their own. 

Today, as I was leaving my house to go to my son's well baby appointment, I wheeled the stroller outside, engaged the brakes (I triple checked to make sure that they were in fact engaged, and applied more pressure to ensure that they would stay engaged). I turned my back to lock the door,and a few seconds later I heard a thunk followed by crying. Apparently, the stroller rolled backwards off of the porch and fell over onto the grass with my son still strapped into the stroller. Additionally, it took me far too long to remove him from the stroller. The belt clips would
not release, and just as I was about to quit and get scissors, I was able to undo the belt and remove him. He was examined thoroughly at his appointment, and fortunately is uninjured.

After the appointment, I left him with his grandmother so I could return the stroller. Before returning it, I inspected it to make sure that it was correctly assembled and that all of the pieces were secure. They were most definitely secure and the wheel assembly was correct as per the instructions included with the stroller.
justification: The stroller malfunctioned, leading to an incident where the child fell but was uninjured.

incident_description: The Little Tikes Cozy Coupe 30th Anniversary Edition car falls over...constantly...when my 16 month is riding in it or even outside of it.  Numerous times now, he has been trapped beneath it when it has fallen on him.  We had a Little Tikes Cozy Coupe several years ago, that NEVER did this.  A child will get seriously injured if this causes a child to fall and hit his or her head when the car falls.  Please have someone look into this and correct this problem.
justification: The description mentions the child being trapped beneath the car multiple times, indicating an incident but no reported injury.

incident_description: I went to change batteries in Disney Elsa and Anna Vanity that lights up and sings. The back is meltdown it. The product is getting to hot.
justification: The product overheating indicates a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I noticed the pole of the my children's Frozen play tent was split, and cracked down the middle. I went to take the tent apart and when I was done. I felt little painful pokes in my skin and arm. I then went to check the material of the pole and then realized it was made of fiberglass. So now I have fiberglass in my hands, arms and all over my shirt and pants, from handling the tent pole. If my children, ages 3, 4, and 6, had been handling the poles they would have had fiberglass all over them.
justification: The incident resulted in painful pokes from fiberglass, indicating an injury, and the likelihood is high given the description of fiberglass spreading easily.

incident_description: I had purchased a trike bike for my son, the Smart Trike Bike. He was visiting my parents in Mexico, so he was playing upstairs outside with my dad. My son, 2 year old toddler, got on the bike and my dad was pushing him, so when he pushed him close to the stairs to take him out and go back home, the handles came off so the bike rolled downstairs. My son had a bad encephalic hematona, and had to be taken to the hospital right away were he had to stay for 2 days. He got an xray, and a CT Scan due to the big impact on his forehead and back of head. He also needs follow up with neurologist due to a fluid that comes up in the CT Scan.
justification: The child suffered a severe head injury requiring hospitalization and follow-up care, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: Hi we got my 2year old a little tykes wagon for christmas.I was scared to put him in it cause the side eails will not stay in place.So when we go walking I watch him closely.We were walking to the mail box and gor no reason the wagon wheels just folded backwards under the wagon and it flipped straight forward toward mw thank god cause I waS able to reach down and grab him before he hit the pavement to hard.It scared the mess out of him and myself.He is so upset wondering why I wont let him play with it.I have it put up and will not put him back in it.
justification: The child was not injured but the incident caused significant distress and could have resulted in injury if not for quick intervention.

incident_description: I was pushing my baby in this stroller and the whole wheel just fell off. This stroller was only a couple months old.
justification: The wheel falling off is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: While walking my infant and toddler with the uppababy vista stroller system 2012 model, using the piggyback and bassinet accessories, the stroller tipped backwards causing my toddler to hit his head busting his teeth on the handle bar and nearly ejected my newborn from the bassinet. Had it not been cold and blankets and bassinet cover been used my infant would have been ejected and potentially seriously injured or worse. This system was being used as intended. My concern with this product is an issue of design and weight distribution. The way this product is made the toddler is to hold on to the handle bar while riding on the skateboard like attachment. The problem is no additional weight can be added to he handle bar or the stroller will tip, which is an inherently bad design as that is where a toddler ( most who shift there weight around quite frequently) is supposed to hang on so they do not fall. There is no warning about applying no weight to the stroller or the potential danger of using these two accessories together as liklihood of the toddler tipping it is high and there is no way to secure an infant in the bassinet.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the toddler (busted teeth) and a near-miss with potential serious injury or death for the infant, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (4) due to the inherent design flaw and frequent toddler weight shifts.

incident_description: Disney Pixar "Woody and Jessie" plastic figurines, purchased from Amazon.com. the hats on these items are sharp and cut my grandsons finger, drawing blood.
justification: The sharp hats on the figurines caused a cut that drew blood, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: As I was picking up my younger daughters toys on Friday January 2, 2015 I noticed that one of their toys was missing parts and instead looked rather dangerous. It is a stethoscope from a Disney Doc McStuffins All Better Bath Kit (7pc set) which they just received for Christmas. It was missing the two ear bud pieces and instead there were two sharp points. It did not come like that and we have since found both pieces but I can not let my daughters play with their new toy now since those pieces come off very easy and this toy could damage their ears if they happen to put the ends in their ears without the ear buds on it. I contacted Disney that same day and I have sent them all the information and pictures and they then sent the information to the company who made the toy. I just heard back from them today and although very polite they told me these toys go through all kinds of testing like pull and drop testing and this toy has passed all current safety standards. If that is the case then the safety standards should be updated to also state that sharp objects meant to be put in or near your ears are dangerous and not safe. We have a couple other stethoscopes from other various Doc McStuffins toys/sets and they all have the molded ear sets which are part of the whole unit and not separate. I understand the choking hazard of possible small pieces from these toys but this stethoscope is meant for pretend play and what you do with a stethoscope is put it in your ears. This is not safe for that. The ear pieces did not just fall off and I am going to assume my girls pulled one off accidentally and then saw how easily it came off and pulled the other one off. My concern isn't the pieces coming off easily or not, it is the fact that there are sharp points under those ear buds. The ear pieces should either be one unit with the stethoscope, or at the very LEAST the plastic under the ear buds should be rounded.
justification: The incident describes a potential hazard with a toy that could cause injury, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
My mother bought glow bracelets from Michael's craft stores. The product is made and distributed by Michaels.

As the girls were bending the glow bracelets to activate them, one of them broke and the liquid got into the eyes of my daughter. Since we didn't watch them bend them we thought that they might have bent them too far, however later that night my neice had one break while she was wearing it. Thankfully it didn't get in her eyes although her hands were covered with the liquid.
justification: The incident resulted in liquid from a broken glow bracelet getting into a child's eyes, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: My son received Neon Glow Twister Trax for Christmas and in his eagerness to share, he gave one of the cars to sister. Within seconds, the car got tangled in her short hair and ripped out a chunk of her hair by the root.  As my daughter was screaming in pain with the car stuck in her hair, I attempted several times to shut the car off.  It would not turn off and the wheels kept spinning.  We were only able to free her after her hair had been torn out.  I have serious concerns about the safety of this product.  It takes a large amount of force to rip hair out by the root.  If it had been a shoelace, necklace, or anything else around her neck my daughter could have been strangled.  My concerns are further exacerbated by the discovery that my child is not the first this has happened to based on a quick internet search about this company (Mindscope Products, Inc.).  I would like to make sure that this does not happen to any other child.  My daughter now has a small bald spot on her head.
justification: The incident resulted in a physical injury (hair ripped out by the root) and emotional distress, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to multiple reported cases and the product's design flaw.

incident_description: My daughter received a Robome toy robot for Christmas. The remote requires 3 AAA batteries. Upon installing the batteries, they became so hot within 60 seconds that the battery covers began to melt. We were concerned that the batteries were defective, so installed a different brand. Within 30 seconds they were so hot to the touch that my daughter (8 years old) actually yelled out and dropped it. We havnt attempted to use it again.
justification: The incident caused the batteries to overheat to the point of melting and caused the child to yell out in pain, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Nixie mermaid for christmas. 7 yr old had in bathtub with her and motorized tail caught daughters hair and winded up and inside toy. Had to cut hair to removed toy.
justification: The incident involved a child's hair being caught in a motorized toy, requiring hair to be cut, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
I purchased the hello kitty kitchen cafe at the Target in Stamford, CT as a special Christmas gift for my almost 3 year old daughter. See link below. After putting it together, my daughter started to play with it right away.  Her father and I were playing right along with her as she explored all the the fun and attractive features. One of the main features is the "pretend ice" dispenser on the fridge door. It seems that she reached in the hole to get the ice and as she did so, being a small and curious child, her entire arm, lodge inside the compartment. She screamed for help immediately and began to frantically cry saying it hurt really bad. Her father and I were totally shocked when we saw how tight her arm was jammed in there. We noticed her arm, wrist, and hand start to get red and swell immediately. Luckily the door was easy to snap off even with her arm still in it and we were able to comfort her somewhat by laying her down. The slightest movement caused her arm to hurt even more. Looking at the item from the inside of the fridge door, you will notice that the way the mechanism inside the dispenser is built, it is meant to hold the ice in place by two little flaps that get released downward once the button is pressed to let the ice pass through. Once the button is released the flaps snap back into place so it made it impossible for us to simply slide her arm up as that was causing more tension and pressure. She happened to be wearing a gold bracelet on that wrist that got caught in the mechanism and made it all the worse to release her. We almost called 911 in desperation because we simply couldn't get it out.  To make matters worse, she has a cyst on her wrist that we feared could have burst from the pressure. It would have caused her a tremendous amount of pain and a trip to the ER to get it surgically removed.  It took almost 10 minutes and a bottle of oil to dislodge her arm. Needless to say, she was traumatized and asked me to remove the kitchen from her room immediately as she was very afraid. This product is dangerous!!!!!  Any other child, bigger, or smaller could get their arm caught inside and suffer he same type of injury.  I called the manufacturer and left a voicemail and wrote an email because they are closed on weekends. I plan on calling back today to place and official complaint.  I spoke to a supervisor name [REDACTED] at the Target in Stamford, CT and she seemed concerned but explained that she is not familiar with the procedure on how to get an item removed from store shelves and that she would have to get back to me. ( she did not even write my number down). I said I will personally ask for her today when I go return the kitchen to see if she followed up.  Please help me keep my child and other children safe. Target is the #1 place that I prefer to shop for my family's needs and I would hate to never go back if I see this toy on the shelf again.

http://www.target.com/p/hello-kitty-kitchen-cafe/-/A-15432490
justification: The child suffered immediate pain, swelling, and potential risk to a wrist cyst, indicating an injury without long-term consequences.

incident_description:
Item #: BGX70
Hot Wheels Track Builder Rocket Launcher Stunt Pack 
 
MSRP: $4.99
Appropriate for: 4Y+

Child age 5 1/2 years inserted his thumb "inside" bottom of the "rocket"...thumb got stuck.
Toy had to be "broken" open to remove the "pinched" thumb.  Causing severe trauma to child and thumb. If father or a second adult had not been close, child would been taken to ER to remove. Child will likely lose his thumb nail.  It could of been worse....we do feel at the very least, a warning needs to be on product.  

I did look for a place on the site @ hotwheels.com to make a report...found nothing.  I would think
a company/band the size of Hot Wheels would like to hear directly from their customers.
justification: The child suffered severe trauma to the thumb and will likely lose the nail, which constitutes an injury (severity 3). The incident seems possible but not highly frequent based on the description (likelihood 3).

incident_description: I purchased the Nickelodeon Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Rippin Rider Pogo Stick for my daughter as a Christmas gift.  She put on her knee pads and helmet and went out onto the driveway to jump.  Our driveway is flat and it was a dry, mild temperature day (about 58 deg).  She jumped twice and then proceeded to jump continuously, only making it to 30 jumps before the bolts and spring liberated and the bottom metal piece fell out.  Thank God for her helmet and knee pads, or she could have been seriously injured.  My daughter is 7 and weighs 68lb.  The product states that it is for children 5-9 and 40-80lb.  There is no explanation for why the pogo stick fell apart in under 2 minutes during the first use.  This toy is a safety hazard and I would like to warn other parents, so that they choose a different product if they are interested in purchasing a pogo stick for their child.
justification: The pogo stick failed during first use, but the child was unharmed due to protective gear.

incident_description: We were given a gift today of two Yiboo RC helicopters,  called the Gailwind 314, model UJ314..UPC code 8485760000378. The one helicopter caught fire while it was being charged, it was being charged while sitting on the carpet. It was not near any heat or fire source. It got hot enough that there were actual flames shooting out of the helicopter. We grabbed the helicopter off the floor, and smothered the fire with wet towels. The lithium battery was completely melted on the carpet. Please note, the helicopter sits on skids, the battery was at least an inch off the floor. We took pictures of the helicopter, the carpet damage and the packaging etc.  We will be happy to send you these pictures. This product is not safe and in no way shape or form should be allowed to be sold.
justification: The helicopter caught fire during charging, causing flames and damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I purchased an, "Etna Fire House Play Tent" from Zulily.com on October 30, 2014 and received it on 11/28/14. This was a gift for my son for Christmas and I did not assemble it until 12/28/14. Within minutes of light play by my almost 3 year-old son (who weighs slightly over 30 lbs.) the tent had broken. At first, I thought it had just come apart since the structure is a series of hollow plastic poles that are attached to one another. However, this was not the case and a few of the plastic poles had actually snapped in half leaving both small fragments of plastic and sharp edges where they broke. I could not believe this had happened and was lucky my son was not hurt and that I noticed this immediately. There is no indication of recommended age on the box. I do not think the material the poles are made of are appropriate for this purpose and ends up becoming very dangerous when broken. I contacted Zulily about this, and they did not inform me that they would report this incident. The only other identifying information I have on this item is the UPC code: "084358047337" with a copyright of, "J.S.N.Y. # 4733" and made in China. There is no manufacturer's label or address on this box, nor included within the box.

Thank you and please let me know if you require further information.
justification: The tent broke during light play, creating sharp edges, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I bought the toy for my daughter from Toys R Us. It's Lalaloopsy Color Me ( Squiggles N. Shapes )which they could color or stamped on the doll. After an hour, her eyes were red. She didn't rub her eyes during the time she was playing. The markers that come with the set are toxic since the warning written on the them but small, hardly to be read. The warning "this product contains ingredients which could cause for idiosyncratic responses, such as eczema-type allergic reaction in certain susceptible individuals. If skin rash, sensitization or other allergic reaction occurs, seek medical attention immediately".
justification: The child experienced red eyes, an allergic reaction, indicating an injury from toxic markers.

incident_description:
"Punching" Santa Claus pen/toy sold at PaperSource.

I purchased three of these pens. One arrived with a broken arm and one broke immediately upon use. When the arm breaks, it leaves a dangerous piece of exposed metal stick.  It poked my five-year-old son's fingers, and could easily cause serious injury to a child (particularly if it were near a child's face/eyes).
justification: The incident resulted in injury to a child (poked fingers) and the potential for more serious injuries (e.g., near eyes) is evident.

incident_description: The Flutterbye Deluxe dolls are defective. The doll flies erratically and despite following every safety precaution, the doll flew into my face, hands and leg, leaving cuts all over. Three other people who were with me also received cuts and bruises when the doll flew away from my hand and into their legs. The doll is supposed to be guided by hand movement, as the packaging describes, but instead it will fly erratically. The doll's fingers and wings are very sharp, and the wings also light up,
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries (cuts and bruises) to several people due to the doll's erratic flight and sharp parts.

incident_description: I bought my 2 yrs. old for christmas they toy big hugs elmo . when she was holding it smoke was coming out from the back of elmo which she got burned on her hand. she drop elmo to the floor and run to my crying, I checked elmo and a lot of smoke was coming out, I opened the back and two of the batteries were burned.  I have called to the manufacture and they dont care they just said to go back to the store and returned it. I really feel dissapointed because elmo was the favorite toy of my 2 yrs. old and now she dosent want any of elmo toys anymore.
justification: The child suffered a burn injury from the malfunctioning toy, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of the incident.

incident_description:
Radio Control Rad Racers Speed Series 1:22 scale by Wham-O ages 3+
Manufactured For: Five Below, Inc
Philadelphia PA 19103
MFG Date: 8/15
Batch/Run: 404763 & 404764 & 404765
Made In China

I took the car out of the box and inserted batteries into the remote and the car and gave it to my child to play with inside the hallway of my house, which has hardwood floors. My seven-Year-Old son had operated radio controlled cars numerous times before. The difference between this and his previous cars/trucks was the scale and the type of antenna. His other vehicles antenna were clear flexible plastic tube with a red colored wire running through it. This car has a stiff (resists bending) shiny metal wire with a small coil at the end, for both the remote and the car. Within 2 minutes of his first time playing with this car, he reached down to pick the car off the floor and turn it around, in a narrow hallway with dim lighting. The car's antenna went up his right nostril, caused an immediate cry and a bad nose bleed. The bleeding stopped with the usual head tilted back and pressure from a tissue in a few minutes. I just could not believe this happened immediately after receiving the car for the first time. The antenna is difficult to see from above and also hurts if it whips around. Thankfully it din't protrude into his nose any further or poke him in the eye. Due to the stiff nature of the antenna and difficulty to see it as it whips about anytime the car is picked up, I don't believe the coil at the end would protect a child from injury and is dangerous.
justification: The child suffered a nose bleed due to the antenna, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: 13 1/2 month old grandson playing w toy and got finger stuck in mouth of toy caused purple pinch on index finger took several minutes to get finger out he was screaming incident happened a few min ago
justification: The child sustained a visible injury (purple pinch) and was in significant distress, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
I have a Bugaboo Cameleon Stroller with a seat/bassinet frame part #71101. I have had the stroller for about 3 1/2 years. While I was walking my 3 1/2 year old ~35 pound son the seat frame broke in half causing the frame to break off from the stroller and my son to fall to the ground. After I assisted my son, I looked at the stroller and saw that the plastic holding the parts together had broken in half causing the seat to be unattached to the frame. Luckily, it is winter time and my son was wearing a jacket and did not sustain any major injuries. It does not seem to be a safe design for a stroller to come apart while in use. 

I then contacted Bugaboo and they did not seem to think this was an important issue and did not ever offer a replacement part. There response was "Just like any mobile unit, maintenance and part replacements are sometimes necessary." Which means to me that a stroller breaking in half during normal use is just part of everyday maintenance. Based on their lack of concern, I am led to believe that is may be a common occurrence.
justification: The stroller broke during use causing the child to fall, but no major injuries occurred due to protective clothing. The company's response suggests this may not be an isolated incident.

incident_description: My 7 month old who currently does not have any teeth was playing with the bee rattle from the Parent's bee bop band set. He was chewing on the antennas and one of them came off in his mouth and he started choking on it. He was able to vomit and throw it up to dislodge it from his throat.
justification: The child choked on a small part but was able to dislodge it without injury.

incident_description: I purchased a Nixies Mermaid doll for my daughter, the selling point "it really swims under water". My daughter took it into the bathtub and the propeller that makes the mermaid swim, became tangled in my daughter's hair and I was unable to turn the mermaid off. This resulted in a huge portion of my daughter's hair having to b cut off.
justification: The incident resulted in a portion of the daughter's hair being cut off, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
In November of 2012, I purchased a wooden princess castle for my daughter's 3rd birthday. I selected one that had received very high reviews on Amazon.com and was described by the manufacturer as appropriate for ages 36 months and up. In December of 2013, my daughter (then 4) was toddling near the castle and fell on it, hitting its wooden corner and cutting her chin open to the extent that she needed to be taken to urgent care, where the doctor had to put in 3 stitches to close the wound. I can obtain medical records for this incident upon request. 

I emailed the manufacturer to make them aware of the injury, but received no response (I believe I checked that no response was needed). 

Thinking it was just a freak accident, I continued to let my child use the castle. On December 1, 2014, she again tumbled onto the castle and received a painful cut on her lip, causing significant bleeding. Upon examination I saw it was not severe enough to require medical attention, but it opened my eyes to the fact that the previous incident was not a freak accident, but a dangerous flaw with the toy's design. The castle's wooden edges come together in a manner sharp enough to pierce the skin, and due to its battlement design its edges are numerous.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring medical attention (stitches) and another painful cut, indicating a severity level of 3. The recurrence of similar injuries suggests the likelihood is 4 (likely).

incident_description: I recently purchased the ESPN Air Hockey Table- WM.COM1416003  While playing, the area in the middle that sits above the table (part #5 electronic scorer)  is dangerous. The problem is that it sits too low and if you slide under it with a pusher you slice your hand/knuckles open. I am a very small adult at 4"ft 9" and have small hands and this happened to me. I would be very concerned that it can happen to a child as well.
justification: The user reported an injury (sliced hand/knuckles) due to the design of the electronic scorer, and expressed concern for potential injuries to children as well.

incident_description: 6 year old daughter was using a Flutterbye Flying Fairy as suggested. It was placed on the floor (flat surface). She pushed the button on the launch pad. Despite her hair being pulled back in a pony tail, the Flutterbye Flying Fairy's rotating center caught loose hair near her face, tangling it around the center of the toy. I was able to loosen it some, but ultimately had to cut the hair to detach the Flutterbye Flying Fairy.
justification: The incident involved hair entanglement requiring cutting, but no physical injury occurred.

incident_description: The connector on the seat belt restraint was snapped off when it got stuck in the "elbow" when I collapsex the stroller. Also, my daughter cut  her finger in the crook of the tray when it was to the side and she tried to lift it. I have to say though, the stroller is very sturdy and durable and to this day I would still recommend Graco. Please fix the issue with a parental warning on the product booklet.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut finger, which qualifies as an injury, and the description suggests it could happen again without a warning.

incident_description: Hi, I have an Aprica Twilite Moto travel system. I've had it since around Nov. 2012, purchased from Babies r us. I've used the stroller probably around 20-25 times with the infant car seat attached.  I've used it about 10 times without the infant car seat. A few weeks ago I put my toddler in the stroller, buckled him up, and went to go close the garage when all of the sudden the whole stroller closed up with him in it and fell straight forward. Thankfully, I was right there and unfolded the stroller immediately. He was okay (just freaked out), but his arms were pinned under the tray part when the stroller collapsed, so he couldn't use his arms to guard him from the fall. Luckily, he only got a small red spot on his forehead. I think it was from his face hitting the stroller tray. But it could have been VERY bad, if the stroller would have been near steps, it could have been a bad head injury.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (small red spot on the forehead) and could have been worse, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it happened once in many uses.

incident_description: I went to open the stroller and it pinched my left pinkie so badly that it removed about 1/4 inch of my skin. The wound took several days to heal.
justification: The incident caused a significant injury (skin removal) that took days to heal, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of the stroller mechanism causing the injury.

incident_description: In October 2014, we were pushing our 1 year old daughter in the Graco LiteRider stroller when my husband twisted the handle by accident. About ten seconds later, our daughter started screaming in pain. We soon realized her finger had been caught in the side hinge that releases when the handle is twisted. Her finger was smashed, got extremely reddish purple in color, and was hot to the touch for a few hours. We iced it and it got better as the day progressed so we did not seek medical attention, however it was almost a very serious situation and thankfully we realized what happened as soon as we did and were able to relase the hinge.
justification: The child suffered a smashed finger with visible injury and pain, but no medical attention was required, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident was caused by a specific mechanical action, making it unlikely to occur frequently.

incident_description:
An 18month old child dropped one of the stacking rattles and the rattle shattered and the balls and beads scattered across the floor. The child picked up one of the balls and placed it in her mouth. Luckily, the teacher was able to remove the ball from the child's mouth and sweep up the beads quickly. The beads and balls are a choking hazard.

justification: The child placed a choking hazard in her mouth, but the teacher intervened without injury.

After 2 miles the front wheel popped off causing my baby to do 2 flips forward. Bob customer service was very unsympathetic. A warning if you own this stroller to double and triple check your wheels EVERY time you go out!
justification: The incident involved the stroller's front wheel popping off during a run, causing the baby to flip forward, indicating a potential injury risk.

incident_description:
On 03/27/13 the consumer's daughter got on the seat of the toy and was moving back and forth. The consumer states the toy has purple plastic restraints which snap in the front that were closed while her daughter was sitting on the toy. After approximately 5 minutes the consumer saw her daughter fall on the ground.  The consumer noticed the purple restraints were open. She picked up her daughter from the ground. The consumer states her daughter was crying loud. She noticed a bruise on her daughter's left shoulder and had scrapes on her face. 

The incident occurred outside of the consumer's home where she lived at the time.

An hour after the incident occurred the consumer tried to pick up her daughter by grabbing her daughter's arms and her daughter immediately started crying. The consumer checked her daughter's left arm and noticed the bruise on her shoulder looked worse. The consumer states it looked like a bone was popping out. 

The consumer took her daughter to the ER at Methodist Hospital [REDACTED] located in [REDACTED]. A doctor took X-rays of the shoulder and advised the consumer that her daughter's collar bone broke in half. The doctor wrapped the child's left shoulder and put the child's arm in a sling. The doctor prescribed the child pain medication. The child was released the same day. 
The consumer does not recall the doctor's name who examined her daughter.

The consumer's daughter wore the cast for approximately 6 weeks.

The consumer was contacted by [REDACTED], a representative from Liberty Mutual. The consumer believes the insurance company is representing the distrubutor. The consumer was informed by [REDACTED] that the manufacturer does not have a legal representative. The consumer states she has not contacted the manufacturer since they are located in China. The consumer hired an attorney from [REDACTED] Law Firm to represent her in the legal suit and be the point of contact regarding this incident. The consumer did not have the attorney's information but indicated the law firm is located in [REDACTED].
justification: The child suffered a broken collarbone and required medical treatment, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
I am writing to inform you of an injury caused by the 2013 Baby Jogger City Select stroller. Upon getting the stroller from the trunk of my car, my finger was severely cut when it was pinched in the hinge while unfolding the stroller.  The cut was very deep and painful and took weeks to heal.

I love the City Select stroller but am concerned about safety.  If this could happen to me, it could happen to others as well.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe cut that took weeks to heal, indicating an injury (severity 3). The user's concern about it happening to others suggests it is likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description: Parents of a 2 month old babay were exiting their house going down stairs. The father lifted the carraige by the handle to carry it down the stairs. The father was on the third stair when the handle of the baby carrier broke and caused the baby to hit the ground.
justification: The baby hit the ground due to the handle breaking, which likely caused injury.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern, 

  Below is the email detailing the defect with their stroller, I sent the company GB an email to  info@gbchildusa.com in regards to their GB Ellum Stroller on Sunday, 26 October 2014:


  We recently purchased a brand new GB Ellum Stroller at Babies r' Us at the Pearl City, Hawaii location on Saturday, 18 October.  We saw the product online, read the reviews and decided to look at it in the store before we made a decision to purchase.  We tested the GB Ellum and GB Zuzu floor models in the store both were great products. What we love about it, is it is light weight and compact especially when we travel to the mainland to visit family, which was great.  It is a stylish and easy to maneuver.  Out of the two products we choose the Ellum over the Zuzu.  After a few days of using the Ellum my wife took the baby to his scheduled doctors appointment on Monday, 20 Oct, she was pushing the stroller with our 18 month son in the stroller she got to a curb which she had to lift the front of the stroller to get on the side walk. When she pushed down on the stroller handle to lift the front wheels the right side of the open and fold joint buckled/unlatched, the left side joint held straight. The stroller did not collapse on itself with the baby in, but my wife became concerned when the joint buckled.  She straightened and locked to right side joint and continued to the hospital for their appointment.  When I arrived home that evening she told me of what had happened to the stroller. So I investigated the issue, I pulled the stroller out from her vehicle and unfolded it into its full form, it opened and locked on the full open position with not problem. I then pushed the stroller to see if there was any issues and then applied pressure on the handles to replicate the problem, as soon as I added pressure the right side fold joint buckled, it clicked, and the right side of the stroller from folded a little.  I straightened the right side again the joint locked in and added pressure to it again. Same issue the right side unlocks/unlatches.  I tried to add more pressure on the left side to see if it does the same as the right side but it held straight and locked.  I then got our baby to see if I it would unlock/unlatch if I pushed him to get on a side walk from the a curb.  I pushed him up to a curb and as soon as I applied weight/pressure to the stroller handle to lift the front the right sided unlocked/unlatched.  We then decided to take it back to the store that week. We took it back to the Babies r'us, Pearl City, Hawaii, on Wednesday, 22 Oct, I explained and showed the sales associate the issue and figured the one we bought was a defective item.  So, we were able to exchange it for another stroller of the same kind from the sales floor.  I asked if I could assemble it in the store which was fine with the associate because we did not have another stroller for our baby to use at that time.  As soon as I finished re-assembling the new out-of-the-box GB Ellum stroller. I was doing a quick check to see everything worked I pushed and pulled the stroller to make sure it rolled and turned smoothly, opened and closed the canopy, folded and unfolded the stroller to make sure it folded and opened properly.  I then decided to test the Fold joints and applied pressure to the stroller handles and the right side of the fold joint unlatched/unlocked/buckled again the left side held out fine.  I then showed it to the associate to show her that I was not even putting that much pressure and she tried putting pressure and it did the same thing the right side unlatched/unlocked/buckled .  She then said we had the option of choosing another stroller or getting the same one, we decided to check out strollers in the store but after test other strollers we still ended up wanting the Ellum, so we decided to try it out last time, I figured the last 2 strollers were just a few defective strollers.  So we told the associate we want to try one more time, I picked the box this time and assembled the stroller.  Yet again it does it again the right side joint unlatched/unlocked/buckled. It was then that we figured after 2 straight off the shelf in store strollers there is something wrong with your product not just a few.  I asked the manger if they were going to report this to the manufacturer they said they will inform their higher ups, I took the initiative to inform your company directly.  It is a brand new product on the market with only a few months on the shelf not sure if you have any other buyers report this issue.  I asked the store if anyone else turned in the stroller with the same problems as ours and they said no, not since it was put on the shelf to go on sale, so we were the first.  We love your product but as a concerned parent with a infant I felt that this should be addressed immediately, I will also send an email to the consumer product safety commission informing them of this defect on the stroller that it may collapse if a infant or child is in the stroller.  We ended up purchasing your other product at babies r' us the GB Zuzu it is also a great product, we have not had any issues so far since we exchanged it that Saturday.  The one thing my wife and I have an issue with is comes with the cup holder option but the stroller did not come with a cup holder.  It is the same light weight, compact, easy to maneuver, and stylish stroller as the Ellum, but is is no Ellum, if the issue gets resolved we might get the Ellum or another stroller which is better or the same as the Ellum.  I hope this email helps in resolving any issues with your product and I am standing by to assist and answer any questions that you may have concerning the Ellum stroller.  I can be contacted via cell phone [REDACTED] if you wish to speak to myself or my wife. Mahalo!


Respectfully, 

[REDACTED] 

Ewa Beach, Hawaii
justification: The stroller's joint buckled under pressure, posing a potential hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: My 4 year old daughter was playing with her new toy she received as a birthday gift, it was a sofia the first 6 foot ribbon dancer wand. I, her mother, was watching her dance around the house just as happy as ever. I only left her in the living room for maybe a minute so I could take dinner out of the oven. When I walked into the living room my daughter was standing still, not moving at all, the ribbon was wrapped around her neck, she was turning blue, I was watching my daughter strangle to death, words could never explain that feeling. I picked my daughter up and ran her to the garage where I keep all my scissors. The ribbon was so tight around her neck I couldn't even slip my fingers between the ribbon and her skin,  I slid the scissors in and cut the ribbon. It took a few seconds but she was breathing. She has bruises all the way around her neck but overall she is good. I will always remember this day for the rest of my life, I will never recommend this ribbon dancer wand to anyone.
justification: The child suffered injuries (bruises and temporary strangulation) but survived, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) given the specific circumstances described.

Tip of finger turned purple and baby started to scream and we immediately cut off the string. There were no complications.

My son reach down to grab something from the grass and it toppled over onto our driveway where he then sustained injuries to his forehead, cheek and nose.  The excoriated skin bled and he cried... this product should not topple over so easily..it should be taken off the market or advised that your child wear a helmet and padded suit if used
