incident_description: I know this product has already been recalled, but our Battat Wooden Musical Table's xylophone pegs have loosened and come off the table.  Since this was a choking hazard for our all-too-curious two-year-old, we've taken the table away from her.  Even though this is why the table has since been recalled, I thought I would file a report anyway.
justification: The xylophone pegs posed a choking hazard, but no injury occurred as the table was removed from the child's access.

incident_description:
I received a Peg Perego Skate stroller system as a gift, new. The frame has three height positions, controlled by latches on either side of the frame itself. A bassinet or seat (included with system) locks into these latches. 

The latches on my stroller began popping out of the locked positions while in use (with a baby in the seat). I reviewed the user manual and instructional video to verify I was using the stroller correctly. This problem has occurred on several occasions.

I called Peg Perego and they informed me that the stroller frame could not be repaired, but needed to be completely replaced. For this, I would need a receipt, which I did not have and could not obtain. I was willing to pay for a repair, but this was not an option. The representative told me I would need to purchase a new frame, which would cost upwards of $500. 

The serial number for the product is IP5530NA34FG74ST24
The manufacture date is 2009 12 18  (December 18, 2009)
justification: The latches popping out while in use with a baby in the seat poses a risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Yesterday afternoon around 1:00 p.m. while in the Walmart parking lot in Chambersburg, PA, I was placing my granddaughter in her car seat when she, my wife and I started coughing from an airborne irritant (smoke) inside the car. There was a terrible smell in the car too and looking around to find the problem I saw a small hole being melted in the back side vinyl cover on the driver's seat. I quickly snuffed out the area with my thumb and the melting of the vinyl and smoke stopped. My first thought was there was some type of amber in the air which caught accidently on the car seat cover. Seconds later we started coughing again and I noticed another small hole melting into the vinyl cover and the area was illuminated by some type of light reflection. I snuffed out the area again with my thumb and started removing my granddaughter from the car seat when I noticed again another illumination on the seat cover and followed this source to a mirror on a "Fisher-Price Hand Held Purse-Type Toy". Product number on the toyÃÂs tag says R6796 and 24L4483. Product is made in China. Content of the purse says it contains a polyester fiber batting and cellophane. 
Product Description: It is a look-alike purse toy but not actually a purse. It has a white plastic handle with two colorful disks attached on the handle for a baby to move about. The toy has three cloths leafs attached to the handle that the baby flips about to look at various cloth imprinted pictures on each leaf side. The first leaf's underside has a round bendable reflective mirror.
What I found was that the toy's mirror was reflecting the sun's rays against the back of the driver's seat. The sun was high and bright yesterday when the incident happened and the melting of the vinyl material on the car seat was immediate each time.
Damage to my vehicle's car seat was minor and my granddaughter and I are fine. However, had I been traveling down the road I would not have been able to react so quickly to this situation. It is very fortunate my granddaughter was not injured by the mirror's intense reflection of the sun's rays on her or that we did become overcome by the melting of the seat's vinyl covers while driving!
justification: The incident caused minor damage to the car seat and no injuries, but the potential for harm was significant under different circumstances.

incident_description: The consumer says she assumed it was a drink because of the oranges on the bottle and the bottle looks like a bottle of juice.  The consumer says the words "Orange" are the biggest words you can see on the bottle.  The consumer says that she had placed bottle in the refrigerator.  She did drink some of the contents and spit the rest out when she realized it was not juice.  The consumer is concerned that this may happen to other people also.  She says her throat felt like it had been slightly burned.  The consumer says she is 60 and does use reading glasses.  The consumer feels that the pictures of the oranges are deceiving and feels that children may accidentally consume product.
justification: The consumer experienced a slight throat burn, indicating an injury, and the product's misleading appearance suggests a likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Our daughter was holding the Graco Car Seat Stroller Attachment Plush Doll Toy and the crinkly part on the ear came off in her hands. This could have posed as a choking hazard. I contacted Graco directly, and was told they did not manufacture this item even though it has their name on it. They said it was a licensed product produced by [REDACTED]. When I contacted them, they said they never produced an elephant, and that item was made before their license began with Graco. I contacted Graco back and they basically said they'd give me a coupon to use on another Graco product, which I cannot use...but my concern was for other parents to be aware of this danger. I asked who would report this and let parents know. I was eventually told they would send me a package slip to send the item back to them, but they never sent it. That was in the middle of August. So I am contacting you directly in hopes you can let other parents be aware that the crinkly part of the ear can come off and could pose a choking hazard.
justification: The incident involved a potential choking hazard with no reported injury, and the likelihood is considered possible given the product defect.

incident_description: I have used this stroller for daily walks for about a year. I do no running with it, but occassionally walk quickly to catch up with my husband. Starting at about 7 months of use, I noticed a wobble while casual strolling, that felt like the stroller was trying to turn sharply to the left while being pushed. I checked the tire pressure which was within specs and all tires were the same pressure. I attempted to lube the wheel bearings which did not seem to work. The wobble would come and go, but was more annoying that anything. Fast forward to the beginning of this month, September. I was walking quickly to catch up with my husband when the stroller began shaking violently while on a level surface and almost tipped over due to the wheels lifting off of the ground caused by the shaking. I removed my daughter and checked all the wheels. I then tried walking quickly with the front wheel both locked and in the unlocked position. The condition was still violently present. Once again, the tire pressures are all even and within mfg spec according to the manual. I am not sure what the issue is with this product, but no longer feel safe using it with my daughter inside due to the sporatic and violent condition that occurs.
justification: The stroller exhibited a violent shaking that almost tipped over, posing a risk to the child, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
I buckled my daughter who is 11 months appprox. Weight 21 lbs properly into the stroller with the safety straps propperly adjusted etc .... I did not have hold of the stroller handles and my daughter reached forward while in the seated position and strapped in the stroller. Her body weight must have created an imbalance of the support provided as the stroller teetered on the front wheels and fell forward with my daughter in the stroller. I was able to catch the stroller before her face hit the ground. The brakes were not utilized at this time however this sort of accident must not result in a stationary position with a child in the stroller. 

Make and model: 
Combi - mauve strolee 
Manufacturer # 2450113
justification: The stroller tipped over but the child was caught before hitting the ground, resulting in no injury.

incident_description:
I participated in this recall:

http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml11/11334.html

For this product from Little Tikes:
Home Center Workshop
UPC 0 50743 04174 7
Model: 4174

When I called Little Tikes customer service, they told me the nails were recalled due to the diameter of the nail head being 1-1/4" inches. The new replacement nails would be 1-3/4" inch diameter.

I let the customer rep know that the Home Center Workshop also came with screws that were the same size or smaller than the nails. She told me only the nails were recalled.

I am throwing all the nails and the screws away. If the nails are dangerous, so are the screws that are the same size or smaller. I am writing this report in an effort to warn other parents about these pieces as well.
justification: The recall was issued due to potential hazard, but no actual incident or injury was reported in the description.

Consumer co

incident_description: My daughter was playing on a Kiddieland/Disney Princess Trike. As she tried to get off, she tripped and impaled her face on the sharp castle protruding from the handlebars. She is left with a severe laceration and scar on her face directly above her lip. The Castle with sharp points has no place on a kids toy let alone a bike. After the incident she was rushed to the Emergency Room and underwent reconstructive surgery to close the wounds.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe laceration requiring reconstructive surgery, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such severe injuries from trikes are not common.

incident_description: Older model little tikes drum with attached drumsticks. The drum was stuck(by the drumstick) under a childs jumpy toy. Pulled the drum set out by one of the drumsticks and the caught stick snapped by the string an a piece of the drumstick broke off and is a potential choking hazard.
justification: The incident involved a broken drumstick creating a potential choking hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchased the Cute Expressions Baby Boutique doll from Walmart. This product is marketed for children 3+. My daughter had it on for less than one hour without constant motion from the baby doll. The battery pack in the back became extremely hot as did the doll material and clothing. Thankfully my child did not burn herself. However, I am worried that it could happen to other children.
justification: The doll became extremely hot but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: My daughter tore the little green leaf right off the lion & put it in her mouth & almost choked to death. She's a year and two months old.
justification: The child almost choked to death, indicating a severe incident with potential for death.

incident_description: My daughter was riding the Fisher Price Tikes Barbie lil Trail rider and the four wheeler would not stop. When she first got on she press the buttom on the handrail and started going. She took her finger off the button and it kept going. We had to run and pull her off. The only way we could get it to stop was to unplug the battery.  We were horrified she could have gone into the road because she had no control.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning toy that could not stop, posing a risk of injury, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:

I purchased my Peg Perego Si in Canada, but they are available in the US as well.

incident_description: I, [REDACTED], was playing with the "egg" version of the Splat Ball manufactured by Ja-Ru Inc. and the ball burst dowsing my left eye. The excrusiating pain forced me to ripo my shirt off in hope of whiping the solution out of my eye. This toy only has one choking hazard warning and no way to contact the company who produced it. I don't know about any of the other cases on this site or if there are anymore who would like to join me in a lawsuit upon this company because I have have lost thousands in the past week I have spent at home on the couch in pain from the abrasions to my eye. Feel free to contact me via email [REDACTED].

incident_description: Upon opening helmet for  star wars costume, there was a strong glue odor.  This odor made me feel light headed.  This helmet can not be put on a child's head for them to breathe in the fumes from the glue.  The design of this helmet covers the child's entire head and therefore no air would be circulating inside of it.  There appears to be 4 separate rectangular  spongy/foam pieces glued on the inside of the helmet and this is where the odor is coming from.  Please give your attention to this matter as quickly as possible because halloween is quickly approaching.   Item was purchased online from costume craze.  item number PCG-003-E 221420 B Deluxe kids Clonetrooper Commander Cody Costume sku 883207

incident_description:
The incident involves a brand new Playhut Toy Story 3 Buzz Rocket tent.  This is a childs tent and it has two small pop up side tunnels.  The tunnels are a mesh fabric with metal wires inside for support/structure.  One of the wires broke and was poking out of the side, and scraped my child badly across the face.  It almost scraped his eyeball.

This tent was brand new and there was no wear and tear.  After inspecting it further, we realized there was another part that had a metal wire sticking out.  I think it is of poor design and should be recalled.
justification: The child was badly scraped across the face and the injury nearly involved the eyeball, indicating a significant injury risk.

incident_description: One of my 6 month old twins was playing with a couple toys on the floor.  I heard him cough and gag and looked at him closer.  He had gotten the long cylindrical handle of a plush rattle into his mouth and because it was soft he was able to swallow it half-way down.  Luckily, one end is too large to fit in his mouth, thus stopping it from lodging in...I was able to pull it out by that end.  However, if I weren't there to do that I'm sure he would have stopped breathing.

incident_description:
Orbeez (via The Maya Group in CAl has taken an agricultural/floral industry product and has marketed it as a child's
toy. My grandson received it for his 3rd birthday. Being unusal, I took it to read and understand before "dumping"
it among his other toys. The one he got is with a water tank in which the pellets grow. Yes, they grow in size
according to instructions, but are still very small and very slippery. The box it is packaged in says for 3+,' the
instruction booklet says 5+. Even at that age, I feel the "blobs" are extremely dangerous the young kids. I actually
see no use for this toy. Maya (or actual person responsible for converting to a toy) just exploited this technological
advancement purely for profit. Though that is a way of life and part of our freedom, putting a dangerous toy out is
against all safety concerns of many for years now. I did advise my son (his father) and when he saw what it was and
did, he told me to trash it. Please look ito it, please. A young child could so easily swallow these miniature, slippery
pellets, or slip on them. They ultimately would just be looked at then thrown around, leaving a potential accident
to happen. I have never reported any concerns I may have had about a product. But, when it comes to my
grandkids (and all children), then I must be as proactive as possible. Thank you for listening to my concerns.
justification: The description highlights potential for injury due to swallowing or slipping on the pellets, with a likelihood of occurrence being high given the product's design and target age group.

incident_description: We have recently purchased, the Mega Blocks Fill & Dump Wagon.  My 14 month daughter loves playing with it. However, today while she was playing with it, she had the bucket portion in the dump position and walked away from it. Shortly after her return to the wagon, she tripped over the handle and stepped on the base and caught herself. As she tried to walk away from it, she fell down and started screaming. Her little baby foot was caught in-between the hinged part of the handle that attaches the handle to the base of the wagon. We were unsuccessfully able to remove her foot without cutting through the plastic to release her swollen foot. The hinged portion that appears to be easily removed/popped out would not budge.  We have been unsucceful in contacting the company and felt this may be a potential safety hazard to other jchildren
justification: The child suffered a swollen foot due to being caught in the wagon's hinge, requiring intervention to free her, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My 9yr old son was playing with a disney princess cinderella slap bracelet with his 9yr old friend. He was holding it with his right hand and my son's friend decided to pull on the slap bracelet to take it away from him. When he did that the slap bracelet cut the right palm of my son's hand. It began to bleed a lot. I heard my son screaming and I go investigate. There was a cut from the thumb to the pinky on his right palm. I put some warm water on it to see what the damage was and I had to take him to the hospital. He had to get 9 stitches on his right palm. When I got home from the hospital I found out that the slap bracelet had a piece of metal sticking out of it. I will mail the necessary paperwork to what ever address I need to.

incident_description: The disney 4 in 1 ride on toy has a ring around it to hold younger children on it while rocking or riding. I had to push her body back up (toward the ceiling/seat) and thus freeing her head.  I had to use some force to get her free. She has scrapes on her face, back of her neck and on her arm. The picture may make things clearer.  I can email the pictures, just let me know where. This toy is always in her room and I never though this would happen. Of course from now on it will not be.  My fear is that a child might become trapped in the neck area and strangle.  This toy was rated for 12 to 36 months.  It was bought at ToysRus and is made by kiddieland. It is the disney princess 4 in 1 rideon.

incident_description:
We purchased a doll called the "Heart Glow Baby" which is manufactured in China for the Goldberger Company, LLC of New York. The doll features a valentine-shaped heart which can be removed from the doll's body. The heart glows in different colors when turned on, requiring three small LR44 style batteries. The batteries are secured to the heart with a detachable lid that has one screw in it. 

We have had the doll for a few weeks when one day I noticed the detachable lid on the ground. When I found the doll, the batteries fully exposed. When questioned, no one in the household had purposefully removed the lid. The only conclusion that I could come to was that the screw had become unscrewed by our baby through everyday use and play. 

No one was injured, but I can see 3 situations with potential for injury:

1. A baby eats the batteries - a choking hazard; a toxic hazard.
2. A baby eats the screw that holds the detachable lid on - a choking hazard; other injury hazard.
3. A baby attempts to eat the detachable lid - a choking hazard.
justification: The incident involved exposed batteries and small parts, posing potential choking and toxic hazards, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: My daughter asked me to check the air pressure in the tires of her baby stroller manufactured by BOB Trailers, Inc., 5475 Gage St., Boise, ID 83706. The stroller in question is a ÃÂRevolutionÃÂ model SO13048 (Serial Number AF012319) and was originally purchased new in 2005. This particular stroller has three wheels, one 12-inch from wheel that swivels or can be locked and two rear 16-inch wheels that are fixed. Each of the wheels has a rubber inner tube and a tire. In checking the tire pressure I noted that the larger tires were marked 40 PSI and the smaller tire was marked 35 PSI. All the tires bear the name "KENDA" and are the original equipment on this stroller. Several days after I filled the tires to the correct PSI, as indicated above, I noticed that one of the larger tires was flat. Upon closer examination, the tire had blown off its rim completely on one side. I removed the wheel and removed the tire and tube noticed a jagged hole about a half to three-quarters of an inch about an inch or so away from the tube's valve stem. I surmised that the tire blew out. Looking closer at the wheel I noticed for the first time that it said "MAX. PRESSURE = 30 PSI (206 KPa)." Remembering that I had filled the rear tires to 40 PSI, I immediately reduced the pressure in the one remaining undamaged rear tire to 30 PSI, as indicated on the wheel rim. I also reduced the pressure in the front wheel. I ordered new tubes for all three wheels in the belief that my having over-inflated them might cause them to lose their integrity at a later date. As I was checking out the wheels, I noticed that the inflation pressure information on the tires did not match the information on the wheel rims. In the case of the front wheel, the tire stated 35 PSI but the wheel stated the maximum pressure as 30 PSI. Likewise, the rear tires stated 40 PSI but the wheels stated the maximum pressure as 30 PSI. I was glad to know that the overinflation of the tires was not the result of carelessness on my part and I actually had followed the information printed on the tires. The problem is, of course, that the information cannot be correct on both the tires and their respective wheels. Given that one blew out after only several days or a week suggests that the information on the wheels calling for a lower PSI may be correct. Several things are, I believe, important to consider here. First, these tires and tubes are not like steel-belted automobile tires in which a difference of 5 or 10 PSI might not present much, if any, safety hazard. These are relatively small stroller tires in which a difference of this magnitude does indeed pose a serious safety risk. In the case of the small front wheel, the difference was almost 17% (5/30) and in the case of the rear wheels, the difference was 33.3% (10/30). I am not an engineer and therefore cannot say whether the wheel is not suited for the tire/tube configuration or vice versa. The second important thing to consider is that these strollers are sold as "jogging strollers" and usually are pushed by persons who are jogging, running, or walking at a fast pace. A blowout of a front or rear wheel while the stroller and its infant or child occupant is being pushed by a jogger could easily result in a catastrophic spill with dire consequences for the jogger as well as the child. I would estimate that hundreds of thousands of these strollers were produced and sold in the United States over the past decade alone and many are still in service or will be used again or handed down among family and friends. I have noticed that BOB Trailers still markets the wheels and tires for this unit through an affiliate (http://www.bobparts.com/hpages/bobstroller_parts.html). Current models of BOB strollers on sale at Babies R Us in Fairfax, Virginia, show that the front and rear tires and wheels both state 30 PSI as maximum inflation. I think that my case may reveal a potential safety hazard to others who may still have the same model stroller. I think this matter deserves immediate attention and that the company should recall and replace all the tires and/or wheels, as necessary, to prevent a tragic situation from occurring. Thank you.
justification: The incident involved a tire blowout due to overinflation, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible given the mismatch in tire and wheel pressure specifications.

incident_description:

We don't know how it changed its direction other than the fact that the launch pad does swivel.  Neither my brow or cheekbone were struck leaving the full impact on my right eye.  I almost detached my retina.  I had retinal bleeding, a corneal abrasion, blood pooling from some other part of my eye and general blunt force trauma surrounding my eye.  I suffered (and still do) from excessive pressure in that eye and am currently on two medications to keep it lower (traumatic glaucoma).  It's been two months since the accident and my eye is still dilated as a result of the accident which causes me to have to wear sunglasses for using a computer  and causes me to have poorer vision. The headaches I have from the accident are continuing.  

While I am thankful this did not happen to one of the children present, it certainly could have.  Most likely my injury is permanent.  I coninue to see my ophthamologist and he could not give me a prognosis.  The box for the toy does not show children wearing safety glasses and the print on the outside of the box under "WARNING" talks about a choking hazard.  Under warnings on the website, it simply says "Do not aim at eyes or face" (I did not), and "To reduce risk of serious eye injury or blindness:  Do not shoot rockets at others.  Keep bystanders behind the launch pad."
justification: The incident resulted in serious eye injury with potential permanent damage, including retinal bleeding, corneal abrasion, and traumatic glaucoma, but no death.

As we were pushing the stroller, my son was in the back seat and he put his hand into the space between the wheel and the fender (from the back of the fender, not the outside and not the front).  Because the wheel rotates into the fender from the back when pushing the stroller forward, his hand was sucked into that space between the fender and wheel with enough force to jam his hand in the space and stop the wheel from rotating.  This caused the stroller to swerve to the right and then stop. Once stopped, we flexed the plastic fender to free his hand, which was scraped a bit from the experience.  

There were no injuries other than the scrape, but it's clear that kids can still get their hands into the rotating wheel and it needs to be better protected.
